draft.title: A primitive conversion fails when nested inside a traced broadcast
draft.body:
## Reproducer

Run this example

```julia
using Reactant
f(x) = sum(Float64.(x[1:3]) .+ log.(1:3))
x = Float32[1, 2, 3]
compiled = Reactant.@jit f(Reactant.to_rarray(x))
@assert compiled ≈ f(x)
```

## Observed

On Reactant 0.2.289 the nested broadcast fails during element-type inference. The standalone conversion succeeds.

## Expected

The compiled reduction should match Julia and preserve the element conversion when used inside another broadcast.

## Proposed fix

Construct the unary primitive-conversion broadcast node with the traced TypeCast before nesting it. This keeps fusion and gives inference a callable that accepts traced scalars. The fork implementation is proposed in [PR #3360](https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Reactant.jl/pull/3360).

problems.title: Storing a traced scalar at a CartesianIndex fails during compilation
problems.summary: setindex! of a traced array at a CartesianIndex converted the stored value with the plain element type, which has no constructor from a traced number, so a loop over CartesianIndices that writes one element per step could not be compiled.
